chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what they report, that Allah created Adam in His image. So he said: It is a newly-originated, created image which Allah chose and preferred above all other different images, so He attributed it to Himself just as He attributed the Ka'ba to Himself and the Spirit to Himself.
and He said: 'My House' and [15:29] 'I breathed into him from My Spirit.'

key_terms.اصْطَفَى: chose/selected — the divine act of election, same root as al-Mustafa (the Chosen One)
key_terms.الإضافة إلى النفس: attribution to oneself — a Quranic rhetorical device of honor, as with 'My House' and 'My Spirit'
key_terms.صُورَة: image/form — the created form Allah honored by attributing it to Himself
key_terms.مَخْلُوقَة: created — entirely contingent on Allah, not sharing in His eternal essence
key_terms.مُحْدَثَة: newly originated — occurring in time, contrasted with the eternal nature of Allah

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'Allah created Adam in His image' mean in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim, a close companion of Imam al-Baqir (AS), inquires about the famous hadith — found in both Sunni and Shia traditions — that 'Allah created Adam in His image.' The Imam clarifies that the 'image' (sura) referred to is an entirely created and contingent form; it is not a pre-existent divine attribute. Allah honored this form by attributing it to Himself, using the same possessive language He employs for the Ka'ba ('My House') and the Spirit breathed into Adam (Quran 15:29). This is a rhetorical attribution of honor and distinction, not a statement of divine embodiment or anthropomorphism, and stands as a key Shia theological response to literalist interpretations of this hadith.
